title: World Cup 2026 Hotel Boom Falls Flat as Occupancy Disappoints Across US Host Cities

body:
Hotel owners across the United States had banked on the 2026 FIFA World Cup delivering a windfall of bookings, premium rates, and packed lobbies. With matches spread across eleven American cities, the hospitality industry projected record-breaking occupancy. So far, the boom has not materialised.

Industry data shows that while match-day bookings in host cities like New York, Los Angeles, and Miami have seen upticks, the surrounding dates remain soft. Hotels that raised rates months in advance are now quietly offering discounts to fill rooms, and short-term rental platforms report tepid demand outside the immediate stadium vicinities.

For the Indian diaspora in the US, many of whom had hoped India would qualify for the tournament, the muted atmosphere is compounded by the team's absence from the competition. Travel agents serving the NRI community say World Cup packages to American host cities have underperformed compared to cricket-focused travel, which continues to dominate diaspora sports tourism.

Analysts attribute the shortfall to a combination of factors: the geographic spread of venues diluting demand, inflation-conscious travellers cutting discretionary spending, and the rise of day-trip attendance over multi-night hotel stays. The pattern echoes similar disappointments during the 2014 Brazil World Cup, where hotel revenues outside Rio de Janeiro fell well short of projections.
author: Diaspora Desk
